verdicts.summary: A stale PID file whose PID is now an unrelated live process makes every reconnect fail after 60s, with no automatic recovery.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A managed server is recorded in the pid/port/managed files. 2) The remote host reboots, or the server dies, and the PID is reused by an unrelated process. 3) The user reconnects with RUNNER_CHANGED=0. 4) server_running (tunnel.ts:625-630) is true because kill -0 succeeds and the stat is not Z. 5) wait_ready at 720 fails after the 60s budget, then the script exits 1 at 722. 6) The state files are untouched, so every retry repeats this. Before the change, the branch killed and relaunched after a 2s probe. The only way out is Disconnect, which runs REMOTE_STOP_SCRIPT (tunnel.ts:780-781) and kills the unrelated process.
verdicts.consequence: The connection stays broken, with a 60s hang on each attempt, until the user disconnects. Disconnecting then kills an innocent process.

verdicts.summary: Deleting the map entry before closing makes the finalizer skip the remote stop. That is the intended behaviour, and I found no path where it goes wrong.
verdicts.scenario: Stale entry A is deleted at 1676 and closed. The finalizer sees tunnels.get(key) !== A, so stopRemote is false and it only kills the local ssh process. createTunnelEntry then sets the new entry at 1579. If createTunnelEntry fails, no entry exists and the remote keeps running. A later disconnect stops it via the stop script, which does not need a map entry.

verdicts.summary: The skipped second probe only applies when an adopted PID is known and alive. Otherwise the original probe-and-relaunch path runs.
verdicts.scenario: Tried an external marker with no default runtime file, so ADOPTED_PID is empty. server_running returns 1 on the empty argument, so the 2s wait_ready probe runs and a failed probe clears the state for relaunch. Also tried a managed server whose runtime PID equals the recorded PID. That takes the 671 branch, adopts nothing, and ends at the 711 check.
